Subject: Clarify invoicing currency / taxes for upcoming order form

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. A couple quick clarifications from procurement/billing at NovaCorp before we move this to legal:

- We operate two billing entities (US and EMEA). Can Redwood issue invoices in regional currencies (USD for US usage, EUR for EMEA) on the same order form, or do we need separate order forms for each entity?
- How will taxes/VAT be presented on invoices? We need an explicit appendix that covers VAT reverse charge, withholding tax responsibility, and whether Redwood will gross-up for withholding.
- Preferred payment terms: our finance team prefers Net45 by default — can Redwood accommodate Net45 for Enterprise bookings, or confirm Net30?

Can you provide a short note on the invoice cadence (monthly vs. quarterly) and whether you can split invoices per entity? Also, please attach any tax appendix/redlines you recommend so our tax team can review.

Appreciate it — if easier we can stand up a 30-min sync.

Thanks,

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. High level response below and I attached a draft Order Form + a redline of the proposed tax appendix for your tax/legal teams to review (redline_tax_appendix.docx, Nova_OrderForm_v3.pdf).

Short answers:
- Currency & entity invoicing: We can support per-entity invoicing on a single commercial template by adding entity mapping and invoice remittance fields. Practically this means Redwood will issue separate invoices for each billing entity in that entity's local currency (USD for the US entity, EUR for the EMEA entity).
- Taxes/VAT: Our standard approach is to list taxes separately on each invoice by line item. For EMEA customers we include VAT where applicable; where reverse-charge applies we will mark the invoice as reverse-charge and include the supporting note. Withholding tax: by default the customer is responsible for withholding unless gross-up is contractually required.
- Net terms: Our standard hosted API is Net30. For committed reserved capacity we can approve Net45 on a case-by-case basis with finance signoff (usually tied to credit checks or purchase order cadence).
- Invoice cadence: monthly by default; we can do quarterly invoicing for prepay or advance collections.

Next steps / asks:
1) Kimberly — can you confirm the two redline items we flagged in the tax appendix: (a) explicit reverse-charge language for EU customers, and (b) a short clause on cross-currency exchange rate submission (how we pick a rate and which day).
2) Sam — please confirm whether NovaCorp requires a single PO per global account or separate POs per billing entity. If separate POs are required we will generate separate invoice sequences.

I've attached the two files mentioned and added a proposed schedule for the split-invoicing approach in the Order Form (see section 2.3).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Rachel Kim

Thanks Rachel — quick legal/finance redline notes after reviewing redline_tax_appendix.docx. I left tracked-change comments in the docx but key points below so procurement has something to review in-thread.

1) Suggested clause for tax responsibility (short):
"Each party shall be responsible for its own tax liabilities arising under this Agreement. Customer will be responsible for any applicable withholding taxes imposed by Customer's jurisdiction unless Customer provides Redwood with valid documentation demonstrating exemption. If Customer imposes withholding, Customer shall provide evidence of tax paid to Redwood upon request and shall gross-up amounts only where expressly agreed in the applicable Order Form."

2) Reverse-charge / VAT presentation: include a sentence in the appendix stating: "Where VAT reverse charge rules apply, Redwood will issue an invoice indicating the reverse charge without charging VAT; Customer must self-account in accordance with local law and provide any exemption certificates on request."

3) Multi-currency / exchange-rate handling (new paragraph suggestion):
"Invoices will be issued in the currency of the billing entity. For display or internal reporting purposes, Redwood may show an FX conversion; however, the invoiced amount in the billing currency is the binding payable amount. For any cross-currency settlement where Customer requests payment in a different currency, Customer is responsible for the exchange rate and any bank fees unless otherwise agreed in writing."

4) Net terms language: if NovaCorp requires Net45 we will accept Net45 for this order provided the Order Form references DEAL-3491 and finance completes a credit review. If finance requires a counterparty guarantee or PO cadence, that will be captured in the Order Form special terms.

5) PO / invoice splitting: operationally cleaner to have separate POs per legal entity. If NovaCorp cannot provide separate POs we can accept a single PO with clear remittance mapping, but that will require our billing team to reconcile per-entity consumption monthly which can add an operational lead time.

I attached an edited redline (redline_tax_appendix.docx) with inline comments and the exact clause text. Once NovaCorp confirms whether they will provide separate POs we can finalize the invoice flow and produce an updated Order Form for signature.
